label: Headless E-commerce
description: E-commerce properties using decoupled architectures — a modern JavaScript frontend consuming product data from a commerce API (Shopify Storefront API, Medusa, Saleor, Commerce.js, or custom). These properties share unique SEO challenges around product indexation, faceted navigation, and the tension between dynamic filtering and crawl efficiency.

defining_seo_characteristics.primary_content_type: Product pages, collection/category pages, editorial blog, buying guides, lookbooks
defining_seo_characteristics.typical_conversion_path: Category/collection page → product page → cart → checkout
key_seo_challenges: Faceted navigation generating crawlable URL permutations that waste crawl budget
Thin product descriptions across large catalogs
Duplicate content from product variants (size, color) creating separate URLs
JavaScript rendering of product data affecting indexation speed
Out-of-stock product pages requiring strategic handling (200 vs. 404 vs. redirect)
key_seo_opportunities: Programmatic category and subcategory pages targeting long-tail product queries
Editorial content (buying guides, style guides) bridging informational intent to product pages
Product schema markup for rich results in shopping SERPs
User-generated content (reviews) as unique page-level content
Seasonal and trend-based content for temporal keyword capture

fleet_intelligence_notes.cross_industry_transfer: High within e-commerce cohort. Product page optimization, category architecture, and faceted navigation patterns transfer across all retail verticals. Lower transfer to non-commerce cohorts.
fleet_intelligence_notes.protocol_sequencing_pattern: Typically: Index Diagnostic → Meta Surgeon → Content Opportunity → Link Architecture. Commerce sites often have indexation issues from faceted navigation that must be resolved before content expansion makes sense.

industries.label: Fashion / Apparel
industries.description: Clothing, footwear, and accessories e-commerce. Highly visual, seasonal, and trend-driven. SEO must balance editorial brand content with transactional product discovery.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Transactional and commercial investigation — shoppers browsing and comparing
seo_patterns.competitive_density: Very high — fast fashion giants and DTC brands both invest heavily in organic

industries.label: Beauty / Cosmetics
industries.description: Skincare, makeup, haircare, and beauty product e-commerce. Ingredient-focused content drives informational traffic; product pages capture transactional intent.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Informational leading to transactional — ingredient research precedes purchase
seo_patterns.competitive_density: High — established beauty brands and DTC challengers both compete aggressively on content

industries.label: Health / Wellness
industries.description: Supplements, fitness equipment, wellness products. YMYL territory — Google applies heightened E-E-A-T standards to health-related content and product claims.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Informational with high commercial tail — consumers research health claims thoroughly
seo_patterns.competitive_density: Moderate — YMYL filtering creates a natural moat for sites with genuine E-E-A-T signals

industries.label: Food / Beverage
industries.description: Specialty food, beverages, snacks, and meal kits. Unique SEO patterns around recipe content, dietary restriction targeting, and subscription-driven conversion.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Informational (recipes, dietary guides) funneling to transactional (product purchase)
seo_patterns.competitive_density: Moderate — recipe sites dominate informational but product-specific queries are less contested

industries.label: Home / Furniture
industries.description: Furniture, decor, home goods e-commerce. High-consideration purchases with long research cycles. Room-based and style-based content architecture drives organic discovery.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Commercial investigation — extensive browsing and comparison before high-AOV purchases
seo_patterns.competitive_density: Moderate — Wayfair and IKEA dominate broad terms but niche styles and materials are accessible

industries.label: Consumer Electronics
industries.description: Tech gadgets, audio, smart home, and consumer electronics. Review-driven purchase decisions with strong comparison and specification keyword demand.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Commercial investigation — specification comparison dominates pre-purchase research
seo_patterns.competitive_density: High — Amazon, Best Buy, and review sites (Wirecutter, RTINGS) control the landscape

industries.label: Outdoor / Sports
industries.description: Outdoor gear, sporting goods, athletic equipment. Activity-based content architecture aligns with how users search — by activity, not by product category.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Informational and commercial — activity research leads to gear purchase
seo_patterns.competitive_density: Moderate — REI's content moat is formidable but niche activities have accessible long-tail

industries.label: Pet Products
industries.description: Pet food, supplies, and accessories e-commerce. Emotionally-driven purchase behavior with strong breed-specific and condition-specific content opportunity.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Informational leading to transactional — pet owners research breed-specific needs
seo_patterns.competitive_density: Moderate — Chewy dominates broadly but breed-specific and condition-specific queries are less contested

industries.label: Baby / Children
industries.description: Baby gear, children's clothing, toys, and parenting products. Safety-conscious audience where E-E-A-T signals and trust indicators directly affect conversion.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Commercial investigation with strong safety-informational component
seo_patterns.competitive_density: Moderate — fragmented across many DTC brands with few dominant organic players

industries.label: Jewelry / Watches
industries.description: Fine jewelry, fashion jewelry, watches, and accessories. High-AOV, high-consideration purchases where brand authority and product education drive organic conversion.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Commercial investigation — extensive research for high-value purchases
seo_patterns.competitive_density: Moderate — Blue Nile and established brands dominate broad terms, niche materials and styles offer opportunity

industries.label: Automotive Aftermarket
industries.description: Auto parts, accessories, and aftermarket upgrades. Vehicle fitment is the defining SEO challenge — content and product architecture must resolve year/make/model specificity.

seo_patterns.competitive_density: High for broad terms (AutoZone, RockAuto) but long-tail year/make/model queries are accessible

industries.label: Art / Crafts / Stationery
industries.description: Art supplies, craft materials, stationery, and creative tools. Tutorial-driven content strategy where how-to content is the primary organic acquisition channel.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Informational — crafters and artists searching for techniques and project ideas
seo_patterns.competitive_density: Low-moderate — fragmented market with strong community engagement signals

industries.label: Sustainability / Eco-Brands
industries.description: Eco-friendly, sustainable, and ethical product brands. Values-driven audience where transparency content (sourcing, certifications, impact reports) doubles as SEO asset and trust builder.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Informational and commercial — values-aligned research precedes purchase
seo_patterns.competitive_density: Low — growing but still nascent. Early content moat builders have outsized opportunity

industries.label: B2B E-commerce
industries.description: Business-to-business product sales online. Unique SEO patterns around bulk pricing, specification sheets, and procurement-oriented search intent.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Commercial investigation and transactional — procurement teams researching suppliers
seo_patterns.competitive_density: Low — B2B e-commerce is significantly under-optimized compared to B2C, creating opportunity

industries.label: Subscription Commerce
industries.description: Subscription box and recurring product delivery brands. SEO patterns unique around unboxing content, comparison content, and cancel/churn-related queries that can be recaptured.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Commercial investigation — consumers comparing subscription options before committing
seo_patterns.competitive_density: Moderate — niche-specific. Broad 'best subscription box' queries are competitive but vertical-specific are accessible

industries.label: Luxury / Premium DTC
industries.description: Premium and luxury direct-to-consumer brands. SEO strategy is brand-protective — controlling branded SERPs, building editorial authority, and defending against reseller/affiliate encroachment.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Navigational and brand-investigation — consumers researching brand credibility
seo_patterns.competitive_density: Low for branded terms (if owned), high for category terms dominated by aggregators and review sites

industries.label: Multi-Brand / House of Brands
industries.description: Parent companies operating multiple product brands under one commerce platform. SEO challenge is inter-brand architecture — preventing cannibalization while maximizing aggregate authority.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Mixed — varies by brand and product category
seo_patterns.competitive_density: Varies by brand — the architectural challenge of managing inter-brand SEO is the primary diagnostic focus
